links.outcome: Correct data extraction by GPT-4 versus GPT-3.5 on the same reports against manual reference standard
links.effect: GPT-4 extracted 2631 of 2800 entries correctly (94.0%) vs GPT-3.5 1788 of 2800 (63.9%), P<.001; external reports 90.5% vs 64.2%, P<.001.
links.quote: With 1788 of 2800 correct data entries, GPT-3.5 produced fewer correct data entries than did GPT-4 (63.9% [95% CI: 62.0, 65.6]; range per category, 14%-99%; P < .001).

links.outcome: GPT-4 extraction accuracy on external institution reports versus internal reports
links.effect: GPT-4 extracted 760 of 840 (90.5%) correct entries on external reports vs 94.0% internally; GPT-3.5 539 of 840 (64.2%).
links.quote: For the external reports, GPT-4 extracted 760 of 840 (90.5% [95% CI: 88.3, 92.4]) correct data entries, while GPT-3.5 extracted 539 of 840 (64.2% [95% CI: 60.8, 67.4]; P < .001).

unlisted_practices: Prompt optimization on a development set of reports before evaluating LLM data extraction

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates the performance of GPT-4 vs GPT-3.5 in extracting procedural data from free-text neuroradiology reports without testing an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
